display_title: BT Acquires TalkTalk in Rescue Deal
display_title_he: חברת BT רוכשת את טאלק־טאלק בעסקת הצלה
short_summary: BT has agreed to purchase the struggling broadband provider TalkTalk for £400m, safeguarding 900 jobs while triggering regulatory and governmental reviews.

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.title: BT to buy broadband supplier TalkTalk in £400m rescue deal, saving 900 jobs

paragraphs: In a major development within the telecommunications sector, BT has agreed to acquire the broadband supplier TalkTalk out of administration through a £400m rescue deal. According to the companies, the transaction is expected to save 900 jobs and incorporate an additional 1.5 million UK retail broadband customers into BT's existing operations. The agreement encompasses both TalkTalk and its wholesale division, PlatformX Communications, on a debt-free basis.

However, the acquisition has immediately triggered intense scrutiny from regulators and competitors. The Competition and Markets Authority will conduct a regulatory review of the tie-up. Simultaneously, Lisa Nandy, the secretary for digital, culture, media and sport, intervened by invoking a public interest intervention notice. This step aims to ensure that potential impacts on public health, critical national infrastructure, and vulnerable customers are thoroughly evaluated. TalkTalk provides services to approximately 250,000 vulnerable customers, including elderly and disabled individuals who rely on telecare devices connected to older copper networks, alongside critical national infrastructure providers spanning healthcare, emergency services, and defense.

Rival telecommunications firms have strongly opposed the transaction. Virgin Media O2 criticized the agreement as a stitch-up designed to enhance BT's dominant market share, which currently stands at roughly 30%. Representatives for Virgin Media O2 argued that the arrangement threatens competitive processes and expressed intentions to raise their concerns directly with the government and regulatory bodies.

BT chief executive Allison Kirkby defended the move, characterizing the situation as genuinely unprecedented and stating that millions of citizens and businesses faced severe risks if TalkTalk had collapsed entirely. BT anticipates a £400m cash impact during the current financial year, covering transaction costs, working capital, trading losses, and uncollected revenue from Openreach, which operates as BT's broadband network and TalkTalk's biggest supplier. Meanwhile, administration officials confirmed that all 900 employees will transfer to BT, while both corporate entities will continue to operate separately and compete until the formal regulatory review concludes.

The deal includes TalkTalk and its wholesale business PlatformX Communications (PXC) on a debt-free basis.
